title: Gridkin Scenario File
description: One feature's worth of Gryphon test scenarios against a named GRIFT fixture. Governed by plugins/gryphon_playground/specs/spec-gridkin-v0.md (req-gridkin-scenario-format, req-gridkin-json-schema).

feature.description: Human-readable description of the feature this file covers.

grift_fixture.description: Path (string) or paths (array of strings, in order), relative to the plugin root, to the GRIFT fixture(s) that seed the test database. When an array is supplied, the runner imports each fixture in order; every fixture must import cleanly (result.success && no errors), matching the existing single-fixture contract. Multi-fixture loads are the canonical way to test flows that require pre-existing state, e.g. optimistic-concurrency happy paths where fixture #1 creates an entity and fixture #2 declares a matching entity_expected_version.

soft_delete.description: Entity UUIDs to soft-delete via the service-layer delete_node verb after the GRIFT fixture(s) are imported, before any scenario runs. GRIFT import is additive/upsert-only (spec-grift-v0.md), so soft-deleted graph state is established here. Applied once after the last fixture loads.

covers.description: Spec RIDs / ACIDs this scenario exercises. Required and non-empty — traceability is binding.

inspired_by.description: Required openCypher-TCK mining breadcrumb (req-gridkin-tck-inspiration, req-grid-traversal-lang-tck-mining-3). Either a folder cite — 'opencypher TCK — <folder> (<intent>)', e.g. 'opencypher TCK — clauses/match (...)' — or, where no TCK folder applies, the explicit empty-pass marker 'opencypher TCK — no applicable feature folder (<reason>)' (reason names why, e.g. 'TAP-native: optimistic-concurrency' or 'openCypher TCK has no regex coverage'). 'Looked, found nothing' is a deliberate, recorded state; a missing breadcrumb is a forgotten mining pass. Per-folder COVERAGE state lives in tck-coverage.json, not here. Informational only, never a license claim.

layer.description: GRIFT subgraph return layer to execute at. Defaults to full when omitted.

expected_envelope.description: Path, relative to the plugin root, to the expected response-envelope JSON file.

expected_sql_snapshot.description: Path, relative to the plugin root, to the expected ORM-compiled SQL snapshot file.

oracle_divergence.description: Declares a KNOWN, tracked disagreement between the independent model-based reference oracle (model_oracle.py) and the executor for this scenario, and states why. The oracle check is a third assertion diffing an independent computation of the correct result against the executor's; a genuine disagreement is normally a bug in one of them. This field is the narrow, review-visible escape hatch for a divergence that is deliberate-but-unresolved (e.g. a semantics decision pending a refactor) — never a silent skip. Its value MUST explain the divergence and its resolution path.

expected_error.description: Rejection oracle: the query MUST be refused. Mutually exclusive with expected_envelope/expected_sql_snapshot. The traversal contract includes which queries are rejected, not only which return rows.

type.description: The refusal class: grammar refusal (parse) or semantic/unsupported-shape refusal (execution).

message_contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring the error message must contain — pins the diagnostic, not just the type.
